entries.name: Elijah Madrone
entries.summary: Farm kid, musician, self-taught data guy.

image.alt: Pixel-art portrait of Elijah: a thin, tired man in his thirties with hair grown too long, in a work jacket over a flannel shirt, holding a notebook.
image.credit: Draft portrait, made with PixelLab on 22 November 2026.

facts.label: Called
facts.value: "Mad" by David. "College" by Marta and Lou.

facts.label: From
facts.value: A working farm in Sonoma County

facts.label: Band
facts.value: Second Crop, with Nate on bass and Wes on drums

body: Elijah grew up on a working farm in Sonoma County. His grandmother used to walk him through the hills behind her place and put his hand flat against the madrone trees. "That's your tree," she told him. "It can burn to the ground and come back from the root."

Before the pandemic his life ran on three engines: music, drawing in the hours nobody paid for, and delivery driving. In the dead hours between routes, parked in a lot with his phone propped on the wheel, he started teaching himself to code. It got him to Claypot.

In late 2022 he shows a chatbot to three realtors at [[the-bear-flag|the Bear Flag]]. A week later they raise their glasses to him. That is [[the-toast|the toast]], and the book follows what he does about it. The Monday after, he makes [[the-bet|the bet]].
When he drives north to [[the-co-op|the co-op]], his grandmother's woodstove, [[the-fisher|the Fisher]], is in the bed of the truck.

entries.name: The Bear Flag
entries.summary: David's bar, in the town where Elijah and David grew up.

facts.label: On the wall
facts.value: A little framed prayer, hung behind the register by David's father the year he quit drinking

body: The book starts here. David McGrath rode the same school bus as [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] for eleven years and has been pouring his beer for fifteen. He stopped asking what Elijah wanted a long time ago.
It has sticky wood, a neon bear, and a television nobody watches. David's father sits on the last stool with a club soda and a lime.

In late 2022 Elijah sits at the bar night after night with his laptop, having a chatbot walk him through building software. Three realtors at the corner of the bar look over at his screen. [[the-toast|The toast]] happens on the same stool one week later.

quotes.from: David, to [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]]. "It was their oldest line."

entries.name: The Fisher
entries.summary: A squat black woodstove, older than Elijah.

facts.label: Made of
facts.value: Four hundred pounds of plate steel

facts.label: Came from
facts.value: His grandmother's things, under tarps in the barn at his mother's farm

body: His grandmother heated a whole farmhouse with it. She cooked on it, dried socks over it, and kept lambs alive behind it in bad Februaries, all on wood she bucked herself from her own downed oaks.

In 2023 [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] and Manny, his mother's neighbor, get it up one flight of stairs into his apartment with an appliance dolly. There is no pipe coming out of it. He sits on the floor in front of it to record his video.

It rides north in the bed of his truck with its door wired shut, "like a passenger who didn't care for conversation." At [[the-co-op|the co-op]] it sits under a tarp in the corner of the shed, because there is nowhere to put it.

entries.name: The Toast
entries.summary: Three realtors raise their glasses to Elijah for the three people they let go.

facts.label: When
facts.value: Late 2022, one week after he showed them the machine

body: A week earlier [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] had turned his laptop toward three realtors at the bar and shown them a machine writing code. Then he slid a bar napkin with his email address across the wood. He thought he was handing them a telescope.

One week later, almost to the hour, a hand lands on his shoulder "like a gavel." The silver-haired realtor tells the bar that this guy saved him so much money. They let three people go that week: their transaction coordinator, their marketing gal, and the kid who did their listing videos.
Three glasses go up, catching the neon. Elijah's arm lifts his own. "The beer was cold and tasted like nothing." He says congratulations.
The Monday after, he makes [[the-bet|the bet]].

quotes.text: I just want people to see what's coming.
There was nothing special about these three men except that they'd gotten the demonstration early.

entries.name: The Co-op

facts.label: Where
facts.value: Up past Cloverdale, off the county road

facts.label: Ground
facts.value: The shed, the shouse, the seed house, the packing shed and Irene's forty acres

body: Grace's email to [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] says what it is: "We grow food and fix things and run a kitchen that feeds folks who can't." She also tells him the table is split about him. "Half the table thinks you're right. The other half thinks you're a guy who got famous scaring people. They both come to dinner Friday."
The shed is an old apple-packing shed with a plasma table in it. Marta Okonkwo runs it.

Grace runs the town kitchen and the route. Denny Osei runs the channel. Lou grew pears outside Ukiah and grows most of what is on the table. Curtis drives the route. Priya digs the pits. Reuben Vance handles the part of the machine that runs on paper. Frank Kowalski ran the hardware store and then the tool library. Tyler writes the firmware. Patricia speaks for the grower network. Irene Calder owns the forty acres. Rosa packs fruit. Wren leads the Sunday circle.
Elijah arrives in November 2024 with [[the-fisher|the Fisher]] riding low in the back of his truck.

quotes.text: Co-op. Nineteen households. We make what we can't afford to buy and fix what the market says to throw away.

entries.name: The Bet

facts.label: Between
facts.value: [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] and Devendra, his colleague at Claypot

facts.label: Made
facts.value: Late 2022, at the coffee machine, the Monday after [[the-toast|the toast]]

facts.label: The call
facts.value: "A machine that can do any job in this building."

body: [[elijah-madrone|Elijah]] brings a printout to work and tells Devendra he thinks it is already over. Devendra is senior and calm. "You'll calibrate. Everybody's first month feels like the apocalypse."

Devendra lands a point first. "Three jobs in one bar is an anecdote," he says. "You build models for a living. What's your n?" Elijah doesn't have one. Then Devendra asks him for a date, and Elijah finds out he has one when he says it.
Devendra peels a sticky note off the pad by the sugar, writes on it in small square letters, and presses it to the side of the coffee machine, under the sign about descaling.
